title: Attribute-routed actions with typed results
summary: Mark an API controller, keep the attribute route, and return a typed result with 404 handling.

scenario.briefing: Unknown products are returned as null with a 200 status, and the controller is not marked as an API controller, so model validation and problem details are not enabled. Return a typed action result and a 404 for a missing product.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Keep the existing route template and the integer constraint.
Change the return type to ActionResult<Product>.
Return NotFound() when the service returns null, otherwise return the product.

misconceptions.feedback: A null body is still a 200 response. Return NotFound() explicitly when the service finds nothing.

sections.title: Attribute routing
sections.body: [Route("api/[controller]")] sets the base path, and [controller] is replaced by the controller name without the Controller suffix. [HttpGet("{id:int}")] adds the method and an integer route constraint, so a non-numeric id does not reach the action.

sections.title: [ApiController] changes the behavior
sections.body: The attribute enables automatic model validation, binding source inference, and problem details responses. Without it, an invalid model can reach the action and failures return a generic response.

sections.title: ActionResult<T> carries both shapes
sections.body: An action can return the product or a status result. ActionResult<Product> lets the method return the product directly on success and NotFound() when the service finds nothing, while the framework writes the correct status.

steps.title: Controller semantics

statements.label: [ApiController] enables automatic model validation and problem details responses.
ActionResult<T> lets an action return either a T or a status result.
[Route("api/[controller]")] replaces [controller] with the controller name minus the Controller suffix.
Returning null from an action produces a 404 automatically.
ControllerBase exists to render Razor views.

steps.explanation: The API controller attribute turns on API conventions, the attribute route binds the action, and ActionResult<Product> makes success and failure explicit. A null return is still a 200 response with an empty body.
hints: Review what [ApiController] enables before judging the statements.
ActionResult<T> can carry either a value or a status result.
A null return is still a successful response with an empty body.
ControllerBase is the API base class; Controller adds view support.
